name: Cranklet
subtitle: Capsule machine puzzle game
shortDescription: Turn the brass crank, watch a glossy capsule drop, and crack it open to meet your next toy.
longDescription:
Cranklet puts one big glass capsule machine at the heart of a cheerful collecting game, and a real puzzle game behind it. There are 60 levels in six worlds, each with its own look and toys, and seven kinds of boards that keep asking something new of you. Six Encore levels remix the world bosses for anyone who wants a harder test.

### Seven Ways To Play A Board
- Steer a capsule down a chute of pegs, bumpers and sweepers into the bin.
- Merge matching chips on a shelf into bigger and bigger ones.
- Sort a shelf so every row is one colour, in as few swaps as you can.
- Plan which of three machines to crank when every coin counts.
- Serve customers who each want a particular toy before the cranks run out.
- Keep the crank in the green on tempo levels, then face a boss machine that mixes it all together.

### 120 Toys On A Glass Shelf
Every toy you crack open goes onto a 3D glass shelf: six albums of twenty, from critters and bots to sweets, stars, tides and charms. Missing toys show as silhouettes, and owning the same toy three times earns a gilded ring. In the Workshop, coins buy permanent upgrades such as a lucky dial that leans toward toys you do not own yet.

### Coins Are Always Free
Coins come only from playing: level rewards, a daily gift and streaks, or an optional short video. Coins and capsules cannot be bought with real money and there is no loot box. Drop rates are published in the game (Common 60%, Uncommon 25%, Rare 10%, Epic 3.5%, Legendary 1.5%).

Also in the box: a seeded Daily challenge with a streak, and Rush, 90-second chained rounds with three lives where you chase your best score.
whatsNew: Version 1.0 launch: 60 levels in six worlds plus six Encore levels, 120 toys to collect, a Daily challenge and a high-score Rush mode.
